correctness.rationale: For a nonsquare solution, Fang implies odd n and square sigma(n), while parity of the divisor sum makes sigma(n) even. Thus b=v_2(sigma(n)) is even and at least two. The exact abundancy identity, the complete local 2^b factor in sigma(n), and standard 2-adic LTE yield the strict product bound, least-prime threshold, and explicit formula without finite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The closest full primary paper proves only the square property of sigma(n), nonexistence of even solutions, exclusion of prime powers, and the special implication 3|n => n square. It does not state or imply the sharper b-dependent least-prime bound without the new use of the complete 2-adic local factor. indexed literature and broader searches found no covering statement.

value.rationale: The claim gives an exact structural sieve for a longstanding open divisor-sum equation: nonsquare solutions must avoid the first four primes, and their least prime grows exponentially with the natural 2-adic valuation of sigma(n). This is a motivated reusable lemma rather than a bounded computation.
